title: The death of John the Baptist (29 August)
hookLine: the prophet dies for telling a king the truth

lines: A PROMISE IN FRONT OF EVERYONE.
cards: The party is already loud. It's King Herod's birthday, and around his table sit his lords, his officers, the leading men of Galilee.
Somewhere under his power sits a prisoner: a man who once wore camel hair by the Jordan, whom the king has locked up but can't bring himself to kill.

Then a girl comes in and dances, and the king is so pleased that he makes a promise out loud, in front of everyone: ask me for whatever you want, up to half my kingdom. She goes out to ask her mother what to ask for.

teach.h: IT IS NOT LAWFUL FOR THEE.
teach.b: Mark tells it in his sixth chapter. Herod had married Herodias, his brother's wife, and John had said to him, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife." That's the whole offense.
One sentence, and true. Herodias wanted him dead. Herod didn't, not quite.
Mark gives a strange, honest detail: Herod feared John, "knowing him to be a just and holy man," and liked to listen to him. So the king kept the prophet locked up, and kept coming back to hear him.
Then the dance, and the promise. The girl's mother tells her what to ask for: the head of John the Baptist. The girl hurries back and adds: on a dish.
Mark says the king was struck with sorrow. But he had sworn, his guests were watching, and he couldn't stand to back down at his own party. So he sent the executioner.
Afterward, John's disciples came, took his body, and laid it in a tomb. Notice who is free in this story.
The king has the throne and the power, and he's trapped by an oath he made to look generous. The prisoner has nothing, and he's the one person in the room who said what was true.
The Church calls this day the passion of John the Baptist, the same word it uses for the suffering of Christ.
All his life John went ahead of Jesus, preparing the way.
Catholics see him going ahead of Jesus here, too.

how: On 29 August Catholics keep the Passion of Saint John the Baptist; the Gospel at Mass that day tells his death from the sixth chapter of Mark.

games.q: you're Herod. the girl asks for the prophet's head. you're sorry, but you swore in front of all your guests. what do you do?
o: keep the oath, and send the executioner.
break the oath, and let the room watch you back down.
stall, and hope she changes her mind.
games.why: he kept the oath to save face. in the story, the king is the one who isn't free.

practice: First, Herod's seat: notice something you keep up only because people are watching, a position, a promise, a story about yourself.
Then John's place: bring to mind someone who may need a hard truth from you, and ask what they would need to know first, that you're on their side.
If you pray, ask Saint John the Baptist for his courage; if not, just hold that person with goodwill.

wordCard.voice: Passion, the Church's word for John the Baptist's death: the prophet killed for telling King Herod the truth, kept on the twenty-ninth of August.

orig.note: Greek: it is permitted, it is lawful. in Mark 6:18 John tells the king it is not: οὐκ ἔξεστιν.

carryVoice: Your line: truth cost his head. In that room, the prisoner was the free one. Until tomorrow.
